note: Sort the probe scan — set SCAN_ID from sc-create.

response.guide:
How to interpret the response:
- result.sorted_by — the sort in effect ("Volume desc" etc.).
- result.columns — the scan's columns after the change (when columns were passed, verify the intended set landed; expression columns matching a standard column adopt its canonical name).
- result.results — live results reflecting the change.
- The change is persisted: subsequent run_scan calls on this scan_id will return rows accordingly.

When presenting:
- Confirm what changed (sort, columns, or both) to the user.
- Render the results as a table. Eyeball-verify a sort change with the user if they care: the top rows should match the requested direction.
- Mention that the change is saved for future runs of the scan.

Error handling:
- "no column named X" → the requested sorting_column does not match any column. The error message lists available columns — relay them to the user and ask which they meant. When changing columns and sort together, the sort can name one of the new columns; if the sort fails, the columns change has already landed — retry with update_scan_config sorting-only rather than re-sending columns.
- "columns[N]: ..." → column validation failure at index N, nothing was changed.
- "no standard column is named X" → the display name (without expression) isn't a standard column; the error lists valid names. Either pick one or provide an expression.
- "column X already exists from a filter" → one of the scan's filters already produces a column with that display name, and an expression was passed for it as well. Re-send that column with NO expression to customize it (visibility, position), or give it a different display_name. Do not drop the filter.
- "created by Cortex" → the scan is read-only via MCP. Suggest creating a fresh scan via create_scan.
- "scan X does not exist or you do not have access" → bad scan_id. Suggest get_scans.
